en.title: Minimum Tree Diameter After Deleting At Most k Leaves (Google OA)
en.description:
Given an undirected tree with n vertices. Each operation deletes one leaf, and at most k operations may be performed; at least one vertex must remain after the deletions. Find the minimum possible diameter of the remaining tree (the diameter is measured in edges).

The original site's constraint reads 0 < k < n, but its public example 1 explicitly uses k=0, so the two conflict. This candidate explicitly revises it to 0 ≤ k < n, which keeps the example and matches the meaning of "at most k times"; n=1,k=0 is valid, and the diameter is 0 when one vertex remains. This is an explicit revision by this site and is not presented as an original-site constraint.

Standard input: the first line contains n k, followed by n−1 lines, each containing a 1-based edge u v. The input is guaranteed to be a valid tree. Output one integer. The original site's object-style examples are rewritten here as standard input/output.
en.input: The first line contains n k (1≤n≤100000, 0≤k<n); then n−1 lines follow, each with two integers u v, representing an undirected edge between 1-based vertices. The edges are guaranteed to form a tree.
en.output: Output the minimum diameter obtainable after deleting at most k leaves. The diameter of a single-vertex tree is 0.
en.explanation: See the candidate notes for the derivation, proof of correctness, and complexity.
hints: The kept vertex set must be connected; any connected subtree can be obtained by deleting leaves from the outside in.
Binary search on the maximum allowed diameter D, and check whether at least n−k vertices can be kept.
For even D, look at radius balls centered on a vertex; for odd D, also check the vertex sets centered on an edge with depth r on each side.
